label: input token b or d during the original phase
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter b or d while the original sequence is being read (t < L), at nearly every such step (~98% recall, ~100% precision). It is silent on all other tokens and on the delimiter. d gives somewhat more activation than b (61% vs 39% of mass). Activation is larger for first occurrences and at early positions; activation share drops with t even though the firing rate stays flat across orig_idx. Repeat occurrences of b/d are weaker and sometimes missing. Weak residual firing (~0.6% of mass) shows up in the copy phase when b/d is fed back as an input (e.g. d at recall_idx 1, about 0.15-0.2 of max).

issues: The claim that it fires on about 98% of b/d original-phase steps is wrong. Precision is 0.99997, with only 6 false positives out of 215,149 predicted steps on the test split, so it fires on about 100% of them. The 0.979 figure is recall over all active steps, not the firing rate.

The claim that repeat occurrences sometimes do not fire is not supported. The predicate restricted to in_first==0 has precision 1.0 on 19,901 steps. The test misses also show repeated d at t=0 and t=1 both at 0.86. Repeats are only slightly weaker per step (mass share 0.087 against step share 0.090).

The claim that mass share falls with t is mostly an artifact of fewer sequences reaching high t, since the firing rate is flat across orig_idx. Examples do show a real fall in magnitude at later positions (d at t=0 is 0.86, later d is 0.61-0.78), so the claim is loosely right.

The missed activations are the copy-phase residual already described: 4,700 steps, 0.6% of mass, all b/d fed back as inputs at about 0.15-0.2 of max. That set has precision only 0.026, so it cannot be predicted and is acceptable to leave out of the predicate. The 6 false positives are scattered: a b late in sequences that start with d.
